## Mean-zero noise model {#sec-noise-model}

Measurement [noise](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/model-validation.html#def-noise) is almost always modeled as a [random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable)
$\noise$ with **[mean](expectation.qmd#def-expectation) zero** and [variance](#def-variance) $\varpar$. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->

::: {#rem-mean-zero-parametrization}
#### Mean zero is a parametrization choice

Mean zero is a parametrization choice, not a substantive assumption.
In $Y = f(x) + \noise$, moving a constant from $\noise$ into $f(x)$
changes the split but not the distribution of $Y$,
so the data identify only the sum $f(x) + \E{\noise}$, the mean of $Y$ at $x$.
Requiring $\E{\noise} = 0$ picks the one split in which $f(x)$ is that mean.
This loses no generality when the model for $f$ can absorb a constant,
as any model with an [intercept](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-intercept) can.
It restricts the model only when $f$ cannot absorb one,
as in a regression through the origin.

:::

Mean zero gives one identity, used repeatedly across statistical modeling
and machine learning.
